summary: Repaired the five control-flow frontend defect classes through the shared control-flow path in a100c/frontend/lower_tir.py: (1) early return lowers as a region terminator -- a per-function %ret.active i1 bound at entry, re-bound false at each return site, carried through every region join and loop channel, with the post-return statements relocated into the live branch arm or guarded on the flag (the returned-vs-default semantics); (2) break/continue lower as loop exits -- a per-loop stop channel ANDed into the re-evaluated condition (a counted range with an exit converts to the while form; `while True`+break terminates; exit-free `while True` still refuses located); (3) the while condition's fold marks the body-assigned names runtime FIRST, so `while j < K` with `j += 1` no longer folds to `while True` from the initial constant; (4) Python and/or lowers to the pinned Triton 3.8 semantics (values evaluated in order, constexpr short-circuit, runtime i1 operands combined right-to-left through bit.and/bit.or with broadcast -- vmor added for boolean blocks and the scalar mask/i64 bool forms normalised); (5) the if-construction restores the pre-branch snapshot between the arms, joins every value carried across a branch (one-path assignment keeps the outer binding as the not-assigned side, ConstVal sides materialise under the join name), and the loop close drops channels the body never re-binds, gives outer-defined finals a region-visible identity definition (the `prev = cur` channel copy) and fresh channel inits for values shared with loop-invariant names; plus the grid-model case-layer interpreter's subscript augmented assignment. The repair exposed and fixed five latent defects the new forms reached: constprop reading a stale loop view after its own insertions (refresh moved after each settled swap) and folding through a broadcast of a carried init; copyprop rewriting `ptradd(p, carried-init-0)` to `p` inside the loop; the TIR verifier's region-close rule comparing against post-join bindings; scalar bool constants lowering as u1 GPRs that mixed with the i64 comparison results; and the split-merge path missing the liveout reload (a loop join consumed by the suffix). Owned-operator sweep: all five classes at zero (277 identities, 24 artifacts, 253 refusals all of other constructs). Full-corpus regression: 535 artifacts vs 427 before, ZERO lost, 108 gained. All 33 test files pass; 15/24 owned artifacts execute and compare PASS at 1 and 4 threads (jagged_to_padded_dense [return], cholesky_upper [while], chebyshev [carried-value], lu_factor_info [augmented-assignment] among them); the 9 failing artifacts fail on a deeper, pre-existing staging defect (an in-region reduction's per-chunk partial is never merged when its consumer sits inside the chunk region) that reproduces identically without any control-flow form and on original-census artifacts untouched by this task -- recorded as remaining work.

remaining_work: In-region reduction staging defect (blocks l1_norm_fused_16977248/7f6ce49c and pre-dates this task on original artifacts like fused_l1_normalize_kernel_765f90f7/fused_l1_norm_and_divide_kernel_2d6d4854): a tl.sum/tl.max whose consumer sits INSIDE the chunk region gets no cross-chunk merge -- the stage plan only merges suffix-escaping partials ('no region-exit value escapes into the suffix' makes it ineligible). The consumer uses a per-chunk partial (out = raw x * per-chunk scale). Fix: extend the two-phase/stage-plan eligibility to split the region at an in-region-consumed reduction, or merge the partial at the chunk back edge and re-load it for the consumer pass.
